purpose: Define a non-inferential contract for proving whether an observed implementation StructureTree conforms to an expected Canonical StructureTree.
invariants: Expected and observed StructureTrees remain independent immutable inputs.
Canonical is the expected/reference structure; observed input is evidence of implementation structure.
A mapping is valid only when supplied explicitly by a mapping profile or another declared evidence source.
Names, paths, prose, layout, colors, proximity and projection coordinates MUST NOT create mappings.
Absence of a mapping is UNRESOLVED, not MISSING_IMPLEMENTATION.
MISSING_IMPLEMENTATION requires an explicit expectation whose mapped observed fact is absent.
UNSPECIFIED_IMPLEMENTATION means an observed fact exists but has no explicit mapping to an expected fact.
MISMATCH requires explicit mapping/rule evidence plus contradictory observed structure.
Projection and rendering never alter conformance status.
Every result carries provenance for expected evidence, observed evidence and mapping evidence where applicable.

statuses.MATCHED: Explicit mapping exists and the required observed fact is proven.
statuses.MISSING_IMPLEMENTATION: An explicit mapping or relation rule requires an observed fact that is absent.
statuses.UNSPECIFIED_IMPLEMENTATION: An observed fact exists without an explicit mapping to Canonical.
statuses.MISMATCH: Explicit mapping/rule evidence exists but the observed fact contradicts the required mapped structure.
statuses.UNRESOLVED: The available evidence is insufficient to decide conformance without inference.

node_mappings.description: Explicit identity/implementation mappings between Canonical entries and observed entries.

fields.kind: Explicit evidence kind such as mapping_contract, annotation, generated_binding or manual_binding.
fields.source: Stable source/provenance locator for the mapping evidence.
fields.locator: Optional finer-grained locator inside the evidence source.

relation_rules.description: Explicit rules defining which observed relation dimensions/types can satisfy an expected Canonical relation.

fields.expected_dimension: Canonical relation dimension this rule applies to.
fields.expected_types: Optional list of Canonical relation types this rule applies to. Omitted means any type in the expected dimension.
fields.observed_dimensions: Non-empty list of observed relation dimensions allowed to satisfy the Canonical relation.
fields.observed_types: Optional list of observed relation types allowed to satisfy the Canonical relation.
fields.direction: same or either. Default same. Reversal is allowed only when explicitly declared as either.

explicit_relation_mappings.description: Optional direct expected-link to observed-link mappings. These take precedence over generic relation_rules.

future_input_modules.rule: Language-specific input modules such as Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, C/C++ and SQL normalize only source-proven facts into StructureTree. They do not perform Canonical mapping themselves.
future_input_modules.pipeline: source -> language input module -> observed StructureTree -> explicit conformance mapping -> Canonical conformance report -> projection style -> Scene -> Viewer
